headword: {呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}

definitions.gloss: enemies in the same boat; rivals cooperating
definitions.explanation: Bitter enemies or rivals who are forced to work together toward a common goal; adversaries who must cooperate due to circumstances.

examples.japanese: {競合|きょうごう}{会社|がいしゃ}と{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}でプロジェクトを{進|すす}めることになった。
examples.english: We ended up working on the project with our rival company.

examples.japanese: {政治|せいじ}の{世界|せかい}では{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}はよくあることだ。
examples.english: In politics, enemies working together is common.

examples.japanese: {利害|りがい}が{一致|いっち}したため、{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}で{協力|きょうりょく}することになった。
examples.english: Because our interests aligned, we ended up cooperating despite being rivals.

notes:
ORIGIN: This idiom comes from the ancient Chinese military text 『{孫子|そんし}』 (The Art of War). The states of {呉|ご} (Wu) and {越|えつ} (Yue) were bitter enemies, but if people from both states were on the same boat during a storm, they would have to cooperate to survive.

STRUCTURE: {呉|ご} (Wu state) + {越|えつ} (Yue state) + {同|どう} (same) + {舟|しゅう} (boat)

USAGE: Used to describe situations where rivals or enemies must set aside their differences and work together. Common in business, politics, and sports contexts.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}で{協力|きょうりょく}する (to cooperate despite being rivals)
・{呉越同舟|ごえつどうしゅう}の{関係|かんけい} (a relationship of rivals forced to cooperate)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{敵|てき}も{味方|みかた}も{なく|} (setting aside friend or foe)
・{大同団結|だいどうだんけつ} (uniting for a common cause)
